To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
1) the population likelihood function of Gaussian mixtures has bad local maximas, and 2) EM will converge to these bad local maximas with high probability.

(i) the EM algorithm is likely to find a bad local maximum when applied to a Gaussian mixture with M ≥ 2 components, (ii) the EM algorithm will not converge to a bad saddle point when applied to a mixture of M spherical Gaussians, and (iii) a first-order variant is likely to converge to a bad local maximum.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of learning the parameters of a mixture of Gaussians model from i.i.d. observations.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the EM algorithm is a good algorithm for finding local maxima of the likelihood of mixture models, but not a good algorithm for global optimization of the likelihood of mixtures.

, for the case of M ≥ 3, the EM algorithm with a random initialization will almost surely converge to a critical point of the likelihood function, and the likelihood value of this critical point is almost surely worse than that of the global optimum.
the EM algorithm is not guaranteed to converge to global optimum, but it does not converge to saddle points.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the EM algorithm is not a robust algorithm for Gaussian mixture models.
the EM algorithm with random initialization is not guaranteed to find a global maximum of the likelihood function, and the bad local maxima it finds can have arbitrarily poor likelihood value.

, despite the simplicity of the Gaussian mixture model and the popularity of EM for its estimation, there are still many fundamental open questions about its statistical and algorithmic behavior.
